source_caption:
During the intense physical production of the film, Tom Cruise insisted on performing his own stunts and weapons choreography, a decision that nearly cost him his life. In one critical battle sequence, Cruise and veteran Japanese actor Hiroyuki Sanada were sparring while mounted on mechanical horses. The timing of the scene relied on Cruise’s horse stopping on a specific mark so he could duck Sanada’s overhead sword strike. However, the machine malfunctioned and kept lunging forward, directly into the path of the swinging blade. Relying purely on decades of martial arts mastery, Sanada managed to halt his full-force swing at the very last millisecond, stopping the heavy steel blade just a single inch from Cruise’s neck. The heart-stopping moment bonded the two actors deeply and cemented Sanada’s reputation on set as an absolute master of his craft.

The Last Samurai (2003), directed by Edward Zwick, starring Tom Cruise, Ken Watanabe, Hiroyuki Sanada. A deeply traumatized American military advisor hired to train the Japanese army in modern warfare is captured by the samurai he was sent to destroy, eventually finding peace among them and joining their doomed rebellion against the modernization of Japan.

source_details.synopsis: The Last Samurai is a 2003 American epic period action drama film directed and produced by Edward Zwick, who also co-wrote the screenplay with John Logan and Marshall Herskovitz from a story devised by Logan. The film stars Tom Cruise, who also produced, along with Timothy Spall, Ken Watanabe, Billy Connolly, Tony Goldwyn, Hiroyuki Sanada, and Koyuki Kato in supporting roles. The film's plot was inspired by the 1877 Satsuma Rebellion, led by Saigō Takamori, and the Westernization of Japan by foreign powers.
